text: Plus vigila semper nec somno deditus esto;
translation: Watch more ever, and be not given to sleep.

text: Proximus ille deo est, qui scit ratione tacere.
translation: One who knows how to speak wisely is near to the gods.

text: Conveniet nulli, qui secum dissidet ipse.
translation: Who's out with self in peace with none will be.

text: Utilitas opibus praeponi tempore debet.
translation: Before mere wealth should safety be sought first.

text: Temporibus mores sapiens sine crimine mutat.
translation: The wise may change his practice without crime.

text: Nil temere uxori de servis crede querenti;
translation: Do not trust your wife when she complains about the servants without cause;

text: Saepe enim mulier, quem coniux diligit, odit.
translation: For often a wife hates the woman her husband loves.

text: Sermo datur cunctis, animi sapientia paucis.
translation: Speech is given to all, but wisdom of the mind to few.

text: Dilige sic alios, ut sis tibi carus amicus;
translation: Love others as you would be loved by them;

text: Rem tibi promissam certam promittere noli;
translation: Do not promise what you cannot keep.

text: Rara fides ideo est, quia multi multa loquuntur.
translation: Trust is rare because many people just say much.

text: Atque aliis cum tu bene feceris ipse, sileto.
translation: And when you have done good for others, keep silent about it yourself.

text: Fac tibi succurrant, iuvenis quae feceris ipse.
translation: Let those who have done good for you come to your aid, young man.

text: Ne cures, si quis tacito sermone loquatur;
translation: Do not worry if someone speaks to you in a whisper;

text: Conscius ipse sibi de se putat omnia dici.
translation: He, who is conscious of himself, thinks that all things are said about himself

text: Non eodem cursu respondent ultima primis.
translation: End and beginning often are unlike.

text: In morte alterius spem tu tibi ponere noli.
translation: Do not place your hope in the death of another.

text: Accipito placide, plene laudare memento.
translation: Receive calmly, remember to praise fully.

text: Paupertatis onus patienter ferre memento.
translation: Remember to bear the burden of poverty patiently.

text: Incusare deum noli, sed te ipse coerce.
translation: Do not blame the gods, but restrain yourself.

text: Utque, quod est, serves, semper tibi deesse putato.
translation: Deem yourself poor and you miss being so.

text: Ne sis ventosus, dum vis bonus esse videri.
translation: Do not be vain, while you wish to appear good.

text: Noli homines blando nimium sermone probare;
translation: Do not try to test people with flattery or excessive speech;

text: Fistula dulce canit, volucrem dum decipit auceps.
translation: Sweet sounds the fowler's pipe is to lure the prey

text: Instrue, quo possint inopem defendere vitam.
translation: Teach how to defend the life of the poor.

text: Sic tibi nec cupidus nec avarus nosceris ulli.
translation: Thus you will be known to no one as greedy or covetous.

text: Ignotum tibi tu noli praeponere notis;
translation: Do not prefer the unknown to the known;

text: Cognita iudicio constant, incognita casu.
translation: Those who are known by judgment are constant, those who are unknown is by chance.

text: Pro lucro tibi pone diem quicumque laboras.
translation: For profit, set aside a day for whatever you work.

text: Vincere cum possis, interdum cede sodali;
translation: When you can conquer, sometimes yield to your friend.

text: Obsequio quoniam dulces retinentur amici.
translation: For by yielding sweet friendships are maintained.

text: His etenim rebus coniungit gratia caros.
translation: For by these things, grace binds dear friends.

text: Ira odium generat, concordia nutrit amorem.
translation: Anger generates hatred, harmony nourishes love.

text: Ipse tibi moderare, tuis ut parcere possis.
translation: Governing yourself, so that you may spare your own;

text: Maxima enim morum semper patientia virtus.
translation: The greatest virtue of character is always patience.

text: Conserva potius, quae sunt iam parta, labore.
translation: Preserve what has already been gained by labor.

text: Utilius regno est meritis adquirere amicos.
translation: It is more useful for a kingdom to acquire friends through merit.

text: Mitte archana dei caelumque inquirere quid sit;
translation: Stop inquiring into the secrets of God andinquire what the heaven is

text: Iratus de re incerta contendere noli;
translation: Do not try to argue about uncertains in anger;

text: Impedit ira animum, ne possit cernere verum.
translation: Anger hinders the mind, so that it cannot discern the truth.

text: Fac sumptum propere, cum res desiderat ipsa.
translation: Be quick at opportunity's demand.

text: Ne plures culpent id, quod tibi displicet uni.
translation: Let not many blame what displeases you alone.

text: Nolo putes pravos homines peccata lucrari.
translation: Think not that evil-doers surely win.

text: Corporis exigui vires contemnere noli.
translation: Do not despise the strength of a small body.

text: Victorem a victo superari saepe videmus.
translation: We often see the victor overcome by the vanquished.

text: Adversum notum noli contendere verbis;
translation: Do not contend with the known against words.

text: Lis minimis verbis interdum maxima crescit.
translation: From the smallest words, sometimes the greatest quarrels grow.

text: Quid deus intendat, noli perquirere sorte;
translation: Do not seek by lot what god intends.

text: Quid statuat de te, sine te deliberat ille.
translation: God decides about you without you.

text: Esto animo forti, cum sis damnatus inique;
translation: Be of strong mind, when you are unjustly condemned;

text: Nemo diu gaudet, qui iudice vincit iniquo.
translation: No one rejoices for long, who wins against an unjust judge.

text: Litis praeteritae noli maledicta referre;
translation: Do not repeat the curses of past dispute.;

text: Post inimicitias iram meminisse malorum est.
translation: To remember anger after feuds is the mark of evil men.

text: Labitur exiguo, quod partum est tempore longo.
translation: What is produced over a long time collapses suddenly.

text: Insipiens esto, cum tempus postulat aut res;
translation: Be foolish when time or circumstance demands it.

text: Stultitiam simulare loco prudentia summa est.
translation: To feign stupidity at the just moment is the height of wisdom.

text: Noli tu quaedam referenti credere semper;
translation: Do not always believe what someone tells you.

text: Exigua est tribuenda fides, quia multa loquuntur.
translation: Do not trust those who talk too much.

text: Consilium archanum tacito committe sodali;
translation: Confide your secret counsel to a trusted friend;

text: Corporis auxilium medico committe fideli.
translation: Commit your body's care to a faithful physician.

text: Noli successus indignos ferre moleste;
translation: Do not bear unworthy success with difficulty.

text: Prospice, qui veniant, hos casus esse ferendos;
translation: Look ahead, those who come, these misfortunes must be endured.

text: Rebus in adversis animum submittere noli;
translation: Do not submit your spirit to adversity;

text: Spem retine; spes una hominem nec morte relinquit.
translation: Retain your hope; hope is the one thing that does not abandon a man even in death.

text: Rem, tibi quam noscis aptam, dimittere noli;
translation: Do not let go of what you know is suitable for you;

text: Fronte capillata, post haec occasio calva.
translation: Behind Time's bald, his forehead's thick with hair.

text: Illum imitare deum, partem qui spectat utramque.
translation: Imitate that god, who looks at both sides.

text: Fortius ut valeas, interdum parcior esto;
translation: To be strong enough to live, sometimes be more sparing;

text: Pauca voluptati debentur, plura saluti.
translation: Few things are owed to pleasure, many to health.

text: Ne nulli placeas, dum vis contemnere multos.
translation: Please no one when you wish to despise many.

text: Sit tibi praecipue, quod primum est, cura salutis;
translation: Let your chief concern be your health

text: Tempora nec culpes, cum sis tibi causa doloris.
translation: Do not blame the times, when you are the cause of your own pain.

text: Instrue praeceptis animum, nec discere cesses;
translation: Train your mind with precepts, and do not cease to learn;

text: Arbitrii non est nostri, quid quisque loquatur.
translation: It is not our own, what each man says.

text: Quantumcumque potes, celato crimen amici.
translation: As much as you can, conceal the fault of a friend.

text: Sermones blandos blaesosque cavere memento;
translation: Remember to avoid bland speeches and flattery;

text: Simplicitas veri fama est, fraus ficta loquendi.
translation: Simplicity is the fame of truth, fraud is the lie of speech.

text: Segnitiem fugito, quae vitae ignavia fertur;
translation: Avoid laziness, the sloth of life;

text: Exemplo simili ne te derideat alter.
translation: Do not let another ridicule you with a similar example.

text: Augendo serva, ne sis, quem fama loquatur.
translation: Preserve your reputation, so that the fame of others may not harm you.

text: Munificus facito vivas, non parcus amicis.
translation: Be not a stingy, but be generous to friends.

text: Utile consilium dominus ne despice servi;
translation: Do not despise the useful counsel of your servant;

text: Nullius sensum, si prodest, tempseris unquam.
translation: Do not always believe what someone tells you.

text: Succumbat labor et frustra temptata relinquas.
translation: Let your work fail, and leave your efforts unavailing.

text: Ne videare malos imitari velle tacendo.
translation: Do not seem to wish to imitate the wicked by being silent.

text: Ipsae etiam leges cupiunt, ut iure rogentur.
translation: The laws themselves wish to be appealed to justly.

text: Cumque reus tibi sis, ipsum te iudice damna.
translation: When you are the accused, let your own judge be your enemy.

text: Multa legas facito, perlectis neglege multa;
translation: Read many things, but neglect many after reading;

text: Ne dicare loquax, cum vis urbanus haberi.
translation: Do not be a chatterbox, when you wish to be considered refined.

text: Coniugis iratae noli tu verba timere;
translation: Do not fear the words of an angry spouse;

text: Utere quaesitis, sed ne videaris abuti;
translation: Use what you have, but do not abuse it;

text: Dilige non aegra caros pietate parentes.
translation: Love your dear parents, but not with a morbid piety.

text: Quas qui suscipiunt, mendicant semper avari.
translation: Those who take on burdens are always greedy beggars.

text: Noli fortunam, quae non est, dicere caecam.
translation: Do not call fortune blind, which is not so;

text: Quam nemo sanctus nec honestus captat habere.
translation: It is what no saint or honest man seeks to have.

text: Aeger dives habet nummos, se non habet ipsum.
translation: The sick rich man has money, but he does not have himself.

text: Fer patris imperium, cum verbis exit in iram.
translation: Bear your father's command, when it leads him to anger.

text: Namque solent, primo quae sunt neglecta, nocere.
translation: For what is neglected at first tends to do harm later.

text: Indulgere gulae noli, quae ventris amica est.
translation: Do not indulge in gluttony, a friend of the stomach.

text: Unum praecipue tibi plus hominem esse timendum.
translation: One thing above all else you should fear is a man.

text: Fac sapias; sic tu poteris vir fortis haberi.
translation: Be wise; thus you will be considered a brave man.

text: Auxilium a notis petito, si forte labores;
translation: Seek help from your friends whenyou are in trouble;

text: Stultitia est morte alterius sperare salutem.
translation: It is foolish to hope for salvation through the death of another.

text: Non tibi fortuna est hominis sed vita petenda.
translation: Fortune is not the essence of a man, but the life is.

text: Utere quaesitis opibus, fuge nomen avari;
translation: Use your acquired wealth, avoid the name of a miser;

text: Quid tibi divitiae prosint, si pauper abundes?
translation: What good are riches to you, if you abound in poverty?

text: Fac fugias animo, quae sunt mala gaudia vitae.
translation: Make your mind flee from the bad joys of life.

text: Ars remanet vitamque hominis non deserit unquam.
translation: Skill remains with a man's life and never abandons him.

text: Prospicito cuncta tacitus, quid quisque loquatur;
translation: Gaze at all things in silence, listen to what each person says;

text: Multum venturi ne cures tempora fati;
translation: Do not worry about the future, the will of fate;

text: Disce, sed a doctis; indoctos ipse doceto;
translation: Learn, but from the learned; teach the unlearned yourself;

text: Propaganda etenim est rerum doctrina bonarum.
translation: Propaganda, indeed, is the teaching of good things.

text: Morbi causa mali nimia est quaecumque voluptas.
translation: Any pleasure, if it is excessive, is a cause of disease.

text: Rursus in adversis melius sperare memento.
translation: Again, in adversity, remember to hope for the best.

text: Discere ne cesses; cura sapientia crescit;
translation: Do not cease to learn; for wisdom grows with care;

text: Rara datur longo prudentia temporis usu.
translation: Rarely is wisdom given through the long use of time;

text: Una dies qualis fuerit ostendet amicus.
translation: One day will show what a friend is like.

text: Non pudeat quae nescieris te velle doceri;
translation: Do not be ashamed to ask to be taught what you do not know;

text: Demissos animo et tacitos vitare memento;
translation: Remember to avoid those who are dejected and silent;

text: Alterius specta, quo sis discrimine peior.
translation: Look at another's condition, and see how much worse yours is.

text: Tutius est multo quam velum tendere in altum.
translation: It is much safer than to stretch a sail into the high seas.

text: Contra hominem iustum prave contendere noli;
translation: Do not try to argue wrongly against a just man;

text: Semper enim deus iniustas ulciscitur iras.
translation: For god always avenges unjust anger.

text: Est iactura gravis quae sunt amittere damnis;
translation: It is a serious loss to lose what is already damaged;

text: Sunt quaedam, quae ferre decet patienter amicum.
translation: There are some things that a friend should bear patiently.

text: Tempora longa tibi noli promittere vitae;
translation: Do not promise yourself a long life;

text: Quocumque ingrederis sequitur mors corporis umbra.
translation: Wherever you enter, death follows with the shadow of the body.

text: Thure deum placa, vitulum sine crescat aratro;
translation: Please, offer incense to the gods, let the calf grow under the plow;

text: Ne credas placare deum, cum caede litatur.
translation: Do not think you can appease the gods with bloodshed.

text: Cede locum laesus fortunae, cede potenti;
translation: Yield your place when injured by fortune, yield to the powerful;

text: Laedere qui potuit, prodesse aliquando valebit.
translation: He who could harm will be able to help at some point.

text: Vulnera dum sanas, dolor est medicina doloris.
translation: While you heal wounds, pain is the medicine of pain.

text: Mutavit mores, sed pignora prima memento.
translation: Even if you changed your way, remember the first pledges.

text: Ne nomen subeas quod dicitur officiperdi.
translation: Lest on you fall the shame that ingrates bear.

text: Ne rursus quaeras quae iam neglexeris ante.
translation: Do not seek again what you have already neglected before.

text: Felices obeunt quorum sine crimine vita est.
translation: Happy are those whose life is without crime.

text: Vitandum ducas inimicum nomen amici.
translation: Consider the name of a friend as an enemy to be avoided.

text: Fac discas multa, vita nil discere velle.
translation: Learn many things; for in life, do not refuse to learn.

text: Miraris verbis nudis me scribere versus?
translation: Are you surprised that I write verses with bare words?

text: Sit brevis, aut nullus, tibi somnus meridianus.
translation: Take a short afternoon nap, or none at all.

text: Ex magna coena stomacho fit maxima poena.
translation: A large dinner causes great distress to the stomach.

text: Vina probantur odore, sapore, nitore, colore.
translation: Wines should be tested for smell, taste, brightness, and color.

text: De qua potetur, stomachus, non inde gravetur.
translation: Let the stomach not be burdened by what you drink.

text: Autumni fructus caveas, ne sint tibi luctus.
translation: In autumn beware that fruits do not become cause for mourning.

text: De mensa sume quantum vis tempore brumae.
translation: Eat as much as you like in winter.

text: Salvia cum ruta faciunt tibi pocula tuta;
translation: Sage combined with rue makes your drinks safe.

text: Non comedas crustam, choleram quia gignit adustam.
translation: Do not eat the crust, since it causes burning choler.

text: Ilia porcorum bona sunt, mala sunt reliquorum.
translation: The intestines of pigs are good; those of other animals are bad.

text: Impedit urinam mustum, solvit cito ventrem.
translation: Unfermented wine interferes with urination, yet acts as a laxative.

text: Hepatis emphraxin, splenis generat, lapidemque.
translation: It (=must) causes stoppage of the liver and spleen, and engenders kidney stone.

text: Sunt nutritivae multum cames vitulinae.
translation: Veal is highly nourishing.

text: Lenit et humectat, solvit sine febre butyrum.
translation: Butter softens, moistens, and acts as a laxative without inducing fever.

text: Unica nux prodest, nocet altera, tertia mors est.
translation: One kind of nut is good, a second is harmful, a third kind brings death.

text: Cruda gravant stomachum, relevant pyra cocta gravatum.
translation: Raw they (=pears) aggravate the stomach; cooked, pears relieve the aggravation.

text: Post pyra da potum: post poma vade cacatum.
translation: After the pear, drink wine; after the apple empty your bowels.

text: Infrigidant, laxant, multum prosunt tibi pruna.
translation: Plums are quite beneficial to you: they are cooling and cathartic.

text: Passula non spleni, tussi valet, est bona reni.
translation: Raisins are bad for the spleen, but good for a cough or for the kidneys.

text: Scrofa, tumor, glandes, ficus cataplasmate cedunt.
translation: Fig in a poultice removes scrofula, tumor, and glandulas.

text: Iunge papaver ei, confracta fans tenet ossa.
translation: Add poppy to it, and it helps to mend broken bones.

text: Pediculos veneremque facit, sed cuilibet obstat.
translation: The fig generates lice and lust, but it resists anything.

text: Provocat urinam mustum, cito solvit et inflat.
translation: Must causes urine, is laxative and brings on gas.

text: Siccos infestat nervos et pinguia siccat.
translation: Harms those of dry humor, and dries up the nerve of the fats.

text: Reddit lingua bonum nutrimentum medicinae.
translation: Tongue (of all animals) gives good medicinal nourishment.

text: Digeritur facile pulmo, cito labitur ipse.
translation: The lung (of all animals) is easily digested and is quickly expelled.

text: Est melius cerebrum gallinarum reliquorum.
translation: The brain of chickens is better than any other animal's.

text: Semen foeniculi fugat et spiracula culi.
translation: The fennel seed loosens gas.

text: Emendat visum, stomachum confortat anisum.
translation: Anise improves vision and comforts the stomach.

text: Copia dulcoris anisi sit melioris.
translation: Sweeter anise is better.

text: Vas condimenti praeponi debet edenti.
translation: The salt dish should be placed on the table at mealtime.

text: Sal virus refugat et non sapidumque saporat;
translation: Salt wards off poison, and adds taste to a man's food,

text: Hi fervore vigent tres: salsus, amarus, acutus.
translation: These three flavors have a warming effect: the salty, the bitter, and the sharp.

text: Alget acetosus, sic stipans, ponticus atque;
translation: The sour, like the styptic, and the acidulous have a cooling effect.

text: Dixerunt malvam veteres, quia molliat alvum.
translation: The Ancients called mallow "malva" because it softens the belly (=alvum).

text: Cur moriatur homo, cui salvia crescit in horto?
translation: Why should a man die in whose garden grows sage?

text: Contra vim mortis non est medicamen in hortis.
translation: Against the power of death there is not medicine in our gardens

text: Cocta facit ruta de pulcibus loca tuta.
translation: When cooked, rue makes the house safe from fleas.

text: Auribus infusus succus vermes necat eius.
translation: The (willow's) juice kills worms when poured into their ears.
